CD117 and tryptase status not reported to exclude mastocytosis

decisive_items: Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm
response.rationale: R3 is supported by extreme leukocytosis and a dermal infiltrate of immature cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, with an immunophenotype (CD33+, CD123+, CD4+, CD163+; CD34-, MPO-, lysozyme-, S100-, CD56-) indicating a monocytic/dendritic leukemic infiltrate. R1 is the closest alternative because of NF1/JXG history and histiocytic markers, but it cannot explain the leukocytosis or blastic morphology. R2 and R4 rely only on annular clinical morphology; R5 is excluded by S100 negativity and CD163 positivity.

rejected.why: Only matches annular clinical morphology; histopathology and extreme leukocytosis are incompatible with erythema annulare centrifugum.
Clinical morphology alone is nonspecific; no mast cell markers (CD117/tryptase) and leukocytosis are unexplained.
S100 is negative and CD163 is positive, excluding Langerhans cell histiocytosis; the immunophenotype is not LCH.
